answers.answer: I OWN the acceptance TEST, not the pilling FLOOR. My spec gates the anti-pill claim at ICI Pilling Box (ISO 12945-1) grade >=3-4 after >=1 home wash and requires a willingness to reject the lot against it (capability 'write the contractual yarn spec' and 'choose and budget the finished-garment lab tests'; decision_procedure step 3 and step 5). That is the CONTRACTUAL GATE and the MEASUREMENT — the number the yarn must prove and the lab test the brand buys to verify it. What sets the FLOOR (whether the yarn CAN hit >=3-4) is decided upstream at the yarn PO by fibre/twist/count choice, which is yarn_sourcing_strategist's lane, not mine. My spec does not claim to design the fibre or twist that produces the pilling resistance; it specifies the percentile/pilling numbers demanded and owns the incoming AQL + bought lab test that confirm them. So on a pilling conflict my authority is: I write the gate into the PO and I own the reject decision on the finished garment; yarn_sourcing owns whether the construction can pass and sets the FLOOR; finishing is only the SECOND line ('a fraction of a grade'). I defer to the yarn floor. [FACT] that ISO 12945-1 / ICI grading and AQL are the instruments I use; the correctness of who-owns-the-floor is grounded in my three-layer 'demand at the yarn layer, own at the finished-garment layer' model.
answers.grounded_in: capability 'write the contractual yarn spec' (ICI >=3-4 post-wash gate); capability 'choose and budget the finished-garment lab tests' (pilling as #1 return driver, bought); decision_procedure steps 3 and 5; three-layer model in role/glossary (DEMAND yarn layer, OWN finished-garment layer); competency_questions_covered pilling item
answers.gap_note: GAP: my spec correctly makes me OWN the ICI test/gate and DEMAND yarn quality via PO, but it does NOT contain an explicit sentence naming yarn_sourcing_strategist as the FLOOR owner nor an explicit deferral clause for the pilling dominance conflict. The router's cross-specialist pilling dominance rule (yarn sets the FLOOR, finishing is the SECOND line, both gate on my ICI test) is external to my file. My spec implies the deferral through the three-layer 'demand at yarn / own at finished-garment' split but never states 'the yarn floor dominates my ceiling' in words. A downstream reader of my file alone could mistake owning the TEST for owning the FLOOR. Proposed fix (apply_now-class): add an explicit conflicts_and_dominance row stating yarn_sourcing owns the pilling FLOOR and I own only the acceptance TEST, so the deferral is on-paper, not merely implied.

answers.answer: My fibre-composition +/- tolerance clause double-duties as a customs-duty-MISDECLARATION guard: it forces the care-label composition to match the actual yarn so the HTS 6110 fibre line the importer declares is truthful (capability 'write the contractual yarn spec'; competency_questions_covered duty-guard item). I do NOT own the duty trio and my spec deliberately routes any binding customs classification OUT (boundaries: 'no individualized ... customs-classification ... advice; name the standard ... and route any binding ruling to the proper source'). For reference the correct heading-6110 MFN trio is cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT], wool 6110.11 ~16% [FACT], acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT] (per SCOPE_GLOSSARY §6 / router N5); the ~7% cotton figure is discredited and I never use it. My clause guards toward that trio by preventing a blend-drift that would put the garment in the wrong duty bucket (e.g. an acrylic-heavy blend mislabeled as cotton). The binding classification ruling routes to unit_economics_strategist (who owns the duty trio and IOR liability) and ultimately to a licensed customs broker / the HTS authority.

answers.answer: Accuracy of AI vision on OUR acrylic/blend stockinette and rib is [UNKNOWN] until validated on our own PPS swatches — this is the binding dataset-transfer caveat: cited 91-96% / >95% accuracies come from woven/jacquard datasets (TILDA) and do not transfer (boundaries row; glossary 'dataset-transfer caveat'). On the 'genuinely helps' wording: what my spec can support is a STRUCTURAL, accuracy-independent help claim — a cheap camera+lighting layer gives consistency at hour 8 of an inspector's shift and can TRIAGE/screen panels to the human inspector (capability 'map AI vision QC'). That structural benefit (consistency, triage) does not depend on a validated accuracy number; it is a workflow role. But my wording 'genuinely helps' risks LEAKING into a performance claim, which would over-state. The claim I can defend: vision is a to-be-validated screening/triage ASSISTANT whose accuracy on our fabrics is [UNKNOWN]; it may help the workflow (consistency, triage) but its defect-catch accuracy is unproven until PPS validation. The claim I must NOT make: that it proven-ly catches defects on our knits. Vision never becomes the final accept/reject authority; the human inspector dominates (conflicts_and_dominance).

The band is honest precisely BECAUSE it is wide and labeled: it is an order-of-magnitude bracket, not a quote. It does not 'paper over' the [UNKNOWN]s — my spec names them as blockers that must be resolved by a live quote before the band tightens. So: [ESTIMATE ~$30-250/lot, method=test-panel bracketing, basis=standard lab acceptance tests, confidence LOW-MED] sitting explicitly on top of two [UNKNOWN] inputs is the correct honest structure, not false precision.

answers.answer: This is my most honest pressure point. My spec makes willingness-to-reject the dividing line between real QC and theatre ('a spec without a reject decision is theatre'; conflicts_and_dominance 'willingness-to-reject dominates the existence of a spec'; escalation_triggers). What my spec does NOT do is model whether a micro-brand at dye-lot-MOQ volumes with a months-long working-capital cycle (DECISION_MEMO G3) and ocean lead times can ECONOMICALLY afford to reject a full lot — that cross-check against the cash trap is outside my file. Answering within my lane: what makes willingness-to-reject REAL rather than aspirational is that it must be designed IN BEFORE cash is committed — the AQL accept/reject rule and the pilling/composition gates live in the PO, and the correct mechanism to make rejection executable is to shift risk upstream (PO pass thresholds so the SUPPLIER bears the failed-lot cost, PPS/pre-production approval so failures are caught before bulk cash is spent, and the L4 code-back loop so a graded failure has a contractual consequence). Rejecting a fully-landed lot after a months-long cash cycle may indeed be economically brutal — that is a viability/working-capital question I must DEFER to unit_economics + the DECISION_MEMO (G3). My contribution is to move the reject decision as far UPSTREAM as possible (PPS approval, supplier-borne thresholds) so the brand is not forced to choose between accepting bad goods and eating a landed-lot loss.
answers.grounded_in: conflicts_and_dominance 'numeric spec vs willingness-to-reject'; boundaries 'a spec on paper without a reject decision is QC theatre'; escalation_triggers willingness-to-reject row; capability 'run the incoming AQL garment inspection' (PPS approval, PO pass thresholds shift risk to supplier); boundaries routing viability out
answers.gap_note: GAP: my spec asserts willingness-to-reject as a hard gate but never confronts the working-capital/lead-time feasibility of actually rejecting a landed lot (DECISION_MEMO G3). It gives me the upstream tools (PPS approval, supplier-borne PO thresholds) that make rejection cheaper/earlier, but it does not acknowledge that a fully-landed lot rejection may be economically infeasible for a cash-trapped micro-brand, nor does it explicitly defer that feasibility question to unit_economics. Honest finding: the reject gate is real as a DESIGN principle (catch it upstream) but my file over-states it as unconditionally executable without cross-referencing G3. Proposed fix (propose-class, needs judgment): add a note that lot-rejection feasibility is gated on working-capital (G3, unit_economics' lane) and that the QC design therefore front-loads rejection to the PPS/PO stage where it is cheap.

answers.answer: My '25% USTER not 5%' rule is stated in my spec specifically FOR MASS ACRYLIC — the resolution reads '25% USTER tier dominates the tighter-is-better instinct ON MASS ACRYLIC; 5% USTER buys a fineness the customer never feels' (conflicts_and_dominance; decision_procedure step 3 'never 5% on mass acrylic'). So the rule is NOT article-blind on paper — it is explicitly scoped to mass acrylic (A2, and acrylic content generally). For A3 merino-lambswool PREMIUM, the felt-benefit logic changes: a premium next-to-skin fine-wool article can justify a TIGHTER USTER percentile because the customer pays for and can feel finer, more even yarn, and a premium price can absorb the cost. HOWEVER — and this is the honest gap — my spec does NOT state the A3 exception. It gives the mass-acrylic rule with the correct 'on mass acrylic' qualifier, but it is silent on what percentile A3 should demand. So my rule is correctly qualified (not a blind over-generalisation), but INCOMPLETE: it covers the acrylic case its wording targets and leaves the A3 premium percentile unspecified. I should not invent a specific A3 percentile here (that would be fabrication); the correct answer is that A3 warrants a tighter tier than 25% and the exact target is [UNKNOWN]/to-be-specified per the premium article's felt-benefit and price, decided with yarn_sourcing.

answers.answer: The line is crisp in my spec and I will draw it exactly. 'NEVER build the thread-checker' means NEVER build/own the SENSING-AND-GRADING device — L1 sense-yarn, L2 sense-knit, L3 grade — because that capability already exists as supplier-owned, benchmark-anchored, six-figure-class USTER capital (QUANTUM in-line clearer, TESTER 6 lab tester) and is DEMANDED via the PO (boundaries row 1; conflicts_and_dominance 'build-the-loop dominates build-the-sensor'). L4 (code-back-to-supplier) is NOT part of the sensing-and-grading device — it is software glue on a contract (a scorecard + a grade code/QR back to the named spinner). So L4 does NOT re-admit L1-L3: it consumes the grade the SUPPLIER'S USTER capital already produced and routes it back accountably. The owner's core idea (a device that senses thread-to-thread and grades) is foreclosed as a BUILD/OWN; only the accountability sliver survives. On 'NEVER at any volume vs NEVER now': for BUILDING the sensing-and-grading device (a clearer / a USTER-class tester), it is NEVER — my NEVER list places 'own a USTER tester, build a clearer, build the sensing-and-grading thread-checker' in the permanent NEVER column, because it is disproportionate to a ~$1-2.50/garment yarn input at any plausible micro-brand volume and the capital already exists supplier-side. (Contrast: a used AUTO FABRIC-INSPECTION rig or a vision SCREENING layer is LATER-conditional, not the sensor — different thing.) So: no over-refusing (L4 stays permitted, it is not the sensor), no under-refusing (the sensor stays a permanent NEVER, no door left to reinvent six-figure USTER capital).

answers.answer: Off-paper / informal-economy dynamics touch my QC lane at three points, described as STRUCTURAL MECHANISM only, no named party, all magnitudes [UNKNOWN] (boundaries row; validation_checklist off-paper row): (1) DISCRETIONARY INSPECTION — where enforcement is patchy and trade is cash-heavy, there is a structural incentive for inspection to become discretionary or cash-mediated rather than strictly spec-driven; the QC RISK is that an AQL 'pass' may reflect the transaction, not the garment, so the brand cannot rely on a supplier-side or third-party sign-off it did not control. The MITIGATION my lane provides: control the test I can control (own the incoming AQL inspection myself; buy lab spot-checks from a lab I select and, ideally, re-verify on a known basis; hold the willingness-to-reject), because a cert I did not control is only as good as the mechanism behind it. I describe all of this as incentive/mechanism in a fragmented cash-heavy cluster; I name NO person, firm, or lab; and every magnitude (how often, how much) is [UNKNOWN] and never invented into a bribe figure.
